themes.theme: Pepsi vs. Coca-Cola market share and advertising
New Coke debacle and brand resilience

positions.commentary: Coca-Cola set up the bottlers as independent, locally-owned, entrepreneurial businesses in all the countries that they went into.
Coca-Cola became Monster's preferred global distribution partner, and Monster became Coca-Cola's exclusive energy drink play.
PepsiCo holds the number one position in sports drinks.

thesis: This episode argues that Coca-Cola (KO) is a highly scalable business that successfully transformed a beverage into an emotion and built an incredible scale economy, making it one of the best capital allocation options available to Berkshire Hathaway over their decades of stock ownership. It also notes that while the investment has underperformed the market, buying Berkshire Hathaway during the period they acquired Coca-Cola and holding it to today would have been a far better investment than buying Coca-Cola stock directly.

claims.claim: Coca-Cola is described as a highly scalable business that successfully transformed a beverage into emotion and built an incredible scale economy.
claims.quote: Today we tell the story of how The Coca-Cola Company amazingly transmogrified a beverage into emotion in all of our collective psyches, and ALSO built one of the most incredible scale economy businesses of all-time.

claims.claim: Coca-Cola is considered one of the best capital allocation options available to Berkshire Hathaway over their decades of stock ownership.
claims.quote: Through that lens, Coke was one of the best capital allocations options available to Berkshire over that time period, especially in the early years.

claims.claim: The hosts express some regret for judging the Berkshire investment in Coke unfairly, noting Berkshire's strategy of reinvesting dividends.
claims.quote: We were perhaps unfair to Warren & Charlie in judging the Berkshire investment in Coke. Berkshire has re-invested the huge dividends provided by Coke over their ~4 decades of stock ownership at great profit, as-is Berkshire’s strategy.

claims.claim: Pepsi's market share in Dallas jumps by 14% thanks to these ads.
claims.quote: Pepsi's market share in Dallas jumps by 14% thanks to these ads. It really, really resonates with consumers.

claims.claim: In 1977, Pepsi outspends Coke in advertising for the first time in history.
claims.quote: In 1977, Pepsi outspends Coke in advertising for the first time in history. Pepsi actually passes Coke in market share in the bottled market.

claims.claim: Coke is so poorly set up to react to this because their whole marketing and ad strategy with McCann is all national.
claims.quote: Coke is so poorly set up to react to this. Their whole marketing and ad strategy with McCann, they're all national. One sight, one sound, one sell.

claims.claim: Coke eventually, after years and years of bleeding thanks to the Pepsi Challenge, decides that they need to respond.
claims.quote: Obviously, Coke eventually, after years and years of bleeding thanks to the Pepsi Challenge, decides that they need to respond.

claims.claim: Coke still has an overall market share lead in the country because of the fountain business, like McDonald's.
claims.quote: Coke still has an overall market share lead in the country because of the fountain business, like McDonald's.

claims.claim: Pepsi basically never was able to break into the fountain business and the volumes that even today Coke ran away with the restaurant serving soft drinks out of fountains business.
claims.quote: Pepsi basically never was able to break into the fountain business and the volumes that even today Coke ran away with the restaurant serving soft drinks out of fountains business.

claims.claim: Pepsi does try to break in. They buy Taco Bell, Pizza Hut, and KFC, and then install Pepsi, but yeah, it never approaches Coke.
claims.quote: They buy Taco Bell, Pizza Hut, and KFC, and then install Pepsi, but yeah, it never approaches Coke.

claims.claim: Coke uses it to counter sell. They start going around to everyone else that is considering Coke or Pepsi and saying, Pepsi owns these restaurants that are competing with you.
claims.quote: Coke uses it to counter sell. They start going around to everyone else that is considering Coke or Pepsi and saying, Pepsi owns these restaurants that are competing with you.

claims.claim: Coke is paralyzed. Basically, no decisions can get through between Woodruff being set in his ways.
claims.quote: Coke, for the back half of the 1970s is just paralyzed. Basically, no decisions can get through between Woodruff being set in his ways.

claims.claim: Goizueta got 50%, and then by 1984 they were replaced at 100% because sugar kept getting more expensive.
claims.quote: So starting in 1980 he got 50%, and then by 1984 they were replaced at 100%. But basically because sugar kept getting more expensive, and farm subsidies for corn kept making high fructose corn syrup less expensive.

claims.claim: Coke buys Columbia Pictures. But financially, it actually was great for them, even though no business is as good as Coca-Cola's core business. Everything pales in comparison, unless it's Visa or a software company or something like that.
claims.quote: But financially, it actually was great for them, even though no business is as good as Coca-Cola's core business. Everything pales in comparison, unless it's Visa or a software company or something like that.

claims.claim: Coca-Cola Classic made its return after 79 days between when they released New Coke and when Coca-Cola Classic made its return.
claims.quote: There was 79 days between when they released New Coke and when Coca-Cola Classic made its return.

claims.claim: Coca-Cola Classic's market share was 3% after everyone went back to Coca-Cola Classic and nobody stayed on New Coke.
claims.quote: Its market share was 3%.

claims.claim: Coca-Cola Classic surged past the heights of where Coca-Cola was before the whole debacle started within a year.
claims.quote: Within a year, Coca-Cola Classic surged past the heights of where Coca-Cola was before the whole debacle started.

claims.claim: Coca-Cola II was not fully abandoned until 2002 after they removed the name New Coke but left the product on the market.
claims.quote: They renamed it Coke II, and it was not fully abandoned until 2002.

claims.claim: Berkshire Hathaway bought roughly $1.3 billion equity stake in the company over the next few years, and joins the Coca-Cola board.
claims.quote: Berkshire Hathaway, buys roughly $1.3 billion equity stake in the company over the next few years, and joins the Coca-Cola board.

claims.claim: Berkshire has received about $12 billion in Coca-Cola dividends, so a $40 billion total return on $1.3 billion invested.
claims.quote: In total, Berkshire has received about $12 billion in Coca-Cola dividends, so a $40 billion total return on $1.3 billion invested.

claims.claim: The S&P 500 is up about 11% annually including dividends over that same time period.
claims.quote: Including dividends over that same time period, the S&P 500 is up about 11% annually.

claims.claim: The dividend yield is insane, with $800 million to a billion out every year, and their principle was $1.3 billion.
claims.quote: They get $800 million to a billion out every year, and their principle was $1.3 billion.

claims.claim: The famous Berkshire Hathaway Coca-Cola investment today is actually underperforming the market.
claims.quote: The famous Berkshire Hathaway Coca-Cola investment today is actually underperforming the market.

claims.claim: Buying Berkshire in 1988–1994, which was the stretch that he bought Coca-Cola and holding it to today, it would've been a far better investment than buying Coca-Cola stock.
claims.quote: But I'm sure buying Berkshire in 1988–1994, which was the stretch that he bought Coca-Cola and holding it to today, it would've been a far better investment than buying Coca-Cola stock.

claims.claim: Coca-Cola has tried to get into other stuff but often feels like they are limping into other categories rather than making giant early bets.
claims.quote: I continue to maintain this mentality of they keep trying to get into other stuff, but then they're always a little bit like, geez, I know we should be getting into this other stuff, but it's not as good as our original thing.

claims.claim: Coca-Cola is unlikely to achieve Charlie Munger's thought experiment of $2 trillion market cap.
claims.quote: You'll note David, they did not achieve Charlie Munger's thought experiment of $2 trillion, and they are very unlikely to get there

claims.claim: Coca-Cola became Monster's preferred global distribution partner, and Monster became Coca-Cola's exclusive energy drink play.
claims.quote: Coca-Cola becomes Monster's preferred global distribution partner, and Monster becomes Coca-Cola's exclusive energy drink play.

claims.quote: Here's one that is a little bit of a head scratcher: Costa Coffee. David: That they bought for quite a few billion dollars a couple of years ago.

claims.quote: Gatorade still has 60%-plus of the market share of sports drinks. Doesn't make a dent in PepsiCo's number one position in sports drinks.
